title: Bounded scratch-template construction
statement: For finite types $Q$ and $T$ with decidable equality, there are a natural number $K$, a finite state set $P$ with decidable equality, a machine $R$ with $K+2$ work tapes over symbols encoding digits, marked work cells, states, or tags, designated states $entry,exit\in P$, and a natural number $C$. For every $k$, embedding $\iota:\{0,\ldots,K+1\}\hookrightarrow\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, Boolean word $x$, natural number $s$, and Boolean word $ws$ whose binary value is $s$, consider a configuration $d$ on the encoded input. If it begins in state $entry$ with input head at position $1$, tape $\iota(1)$ holds $ws$ in the prescribed buffer format on positions from $-1$ through $|ws|$ relative to its head, tape $\iota(0)$ is blank on positions from $-1$ through the length of the joined record template for $x$ and $s$, and all embedded tapes with index at least $2$ are blank, then the embedded machine reaches a configuration equal to $d$ except that its state is $exit$ and tape $\iota(0)$ contains the joined record template on that interval. It does so by some time at most $C$ times the sum of the template length, $|ws|$, $|x|$, and $1$; it does not visit $exit$ earlier, and every work-tape head stays within distance $C$ times the sum of the template length, $|ws|$, and $1$ of its initial position throughout.
hypotheses_covered: $Q,T$ are finite and have decidable equality
Finite state set $P$ with decidable equality exists
Embedding of $K+2$ tape indices into $k$ tape indices
Natural number $s$ and Boolean word $ws$ with binary value $s$
Tape $\iota(1)$ has the prescribed buffer contents on the stated interval
Tape $\iota(0)$ is blank on the stated interval
Embedded tapes with indices at least $2$ are blank
Time bound in terms of template length, $|ws|$, and $|x|$
Final state and template contents on tape $\iota(0)$
